correctness.rationale: Restricting the EPPF to the named labels, adjacent all-one pairs require one triple block; disjoint all-one pairs allow one block of four or the specified two doubletons. Their difference is (1-alpha)(theta+alpha)/[(theta+1)(theta+2)(theta+3)] > 0, also for admissible negative theta. Thus all edge pairs must have the same incidence type. A pairwise-intersecting simple edge family is a star or triangle (an edge avoiding the common end of two incident edges must complete their triangle, after which no fourth edge is possible). A disjoint family is a matching, including the single-edge case. Vertex relabelings realize every edge permutation in all three cases. The sampling-consistent infinite partition on a countable star or matching gives the first two infinite extensions. In a triangle the masses are A at 111, B at each singleton-one word, C at 000, and zero at every two-one word. A uniform k-subset of N gives positive mass to a fixed two-one word exactly when 2 <= k <= N-1, forcing total one count in {0,1,N}. The weights at these three counts are uniquely C-(N-3)B, NB, A; these reproduce all eight words, and the first weight is nonnegative exactly when N <= 3+C/B = (theta+3-alpha)/(1-alpha). This includes equality, N=3, and excludes infinite extension by restriction. The proof holds for all stated real parameters; check.py is a finite corroboration of probabilities, extension weights and small graph shapes, inspected but not executed.
